answer: Clique-density gating. An agent may transact only if its counterparties form a sparse, slowly-growing neighborhood, so a sybil farm's clones would need to buy real edge diversity from established nodes rather than mint it. Each fake identity must then pay a juniper fee in routing latency to reach unrelated clusters, making mass registration costlier than honest trade. Genuine merchants accumulate ember reputation across that topology, while a grove of fresh clones stays isolated and rate-limited.
